name: European Air Quality Index (EEA, 2025 revision)

sources.title: ETC HE Report 2024/17, EEA's revision of the European air quality index bands (3 July 2025), Table 5.2 'Final agreed updated EEA European air quality index' and Table 6.1 health messages

categories.label: Good
categories.health: The air quality is good. Enjoy your usual outdoor activities.
categories.health_sensitive: The air quality is good. Enjoy your usual outdoor activities.

categories.label: Moderate
categories.health_sensitive: Consider reducing intense outdoor activities if you experience symptoms.

categories.label: Poor
categories.health: Consider reducing intense outdoor activities if you experience symptoms such as sore eyes, a cough or a sore throat.
categories.health_sensitive: Consider reducing physical activities, particularly outdoors, especially if you experience symptoms.

categories.label: Very poor
categories.health: Consider reducing intense outdoor activities if you experience symptoms such as sore eyes, a cough or a sore throat.
categories.health_sensitive: Reduce physical activities, particularly outdoors, especially if you experience symptoms.

rules: Each pollutant's hourly mean is rounded half-up to an integer and classified with inclusive upper bounds. The 2025 revision uses hourly PM; the old index used a running 24-h mean.
The index is the worst sub-index across available pollutants.
notes: The index is computed from whatever subset of pollutants is available. Results without PM are flagged 'partial' in the API. EEA's map has its own station-inclusion rules, which we do not replicate.
Open-Meteo's 'european_aqi' field uses its own continuous 0-100+ mapping of the older bands, so it is not comparable with this table. AirAtlas always recomputes from concentrations.
This is the AirAtlas common comparison scale.
